<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-combat-simulation-and-balance-acceptance-plan"></a>
### Combat Simulation And Balance Acceptance Plan

2026-09-09, Plan. DESIGN ONLY, NOT EXECUTED.
Companion to combat-stats-v1, equipment-research-progression-v1,
enemy-ai-wave-execution-v1 and player-input-cooperation-detail-v1.
Acceptance numbers below are proposed investigation thresholds, not measured results
or permission to implement/deploy. No production encounters are enabled here.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-purpose-and-method"></a>
#### Purpose And Method

Replace ideal DPS division with event-driven HP/time trajectories. First verify
rules, then measure balance, then validate the actual client/server presentation.
Do not build a second authoritative balance engine with unrelated formulas: use
the eventual shared simulation core where compatible, or label any planning model
independent and reconcile event-by-event before using it as runtime evidence.

One fixed loadout/config and one deterministic input trace produce one result.
Running identical deterministic inputs100 times proves repeatability, NOT a win
rate. Scenario coverage and later human playtests are separate evidence categories.
No invented random crit/dodge or secret seed affects this baseline; those chances0.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-input-manifest"></a>
#### Input Manifest

Every case freezes caseId, design/config hash, engine revision, encounter and mode,
operator IDs/slots/level/promotion/kit rank, selected ultimate, train level,
legal carriage composition, equipment/research flags, enemy budgets/spawn times,
policy trace, simulation step and observation horizon. Reject missing definitions.
Mark proposals with design-only IDs; never submit those IDs to live APIs.

Initial five: Kyle, Reina, Eve, Sera, Mira. Proposed reference placement:
rear left top Reina/middle Sera/bottom Eve; front right top Kyle/bottom Mira.
This is a TEST lineup, not a mandatory class-slot restriction or new art placement.
Selected ultimate baseline Eve; compare Kyle/Reina/Sera/Mira separately.
Carriage fixtures require a legal total-slot/weight check from actual catalog,
not just per-type max count. Missing loadout-capacity contract = BLOCKED fixture,
not silently accepting all5 devices or pretending no-device train is legal.

Use a minimal legal baseline, legal Gun-focused variant and legal Medical-focused
variant once verified. No new carriage grant/unlock or assumed customer ownership.
Candidate equipment/research stays off in baseline; isolated proposed-modifier
cases may enable it in the planning harness only and must be labeled accordingly.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-growth-and-encounter-matrix"></a>
#### Growth And Encounter Matrix

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-difficulty-and-composition-policy---2026-09-09"></a>
##### Difficulty And Composition Policy - 2026-09-09

User-approved direction: the lowest authored difficulty must be clearable with the
initial/free five; higher difficulties increasingly require well-built specialized
compositions. This is a design requirement, NOT a measured clear result. Lowest
difficulty does not mean level1 clears every late operation: use attainable growth
before that encounter, not its future rewards, with competent non-perfect play.
Do not require initial-five viability at every upper tier or treat that as a failed
balance test. The first-operation level1 fixture below remains the starting case.

Recommended implementation-independent interpretation for the existing five-tier
candidate: I baseline five; II sound growth and defensive timing; III a meaningful
operation-specific role emphasis; IV complementary squad/train specialization;
V tightly coordinated composition and reliable execution. These tier descriptions
are recommendations, not new encounter mechanics or approved numeric multipliers.

Use already authored threats to test role needs, e.g. interruption against sabotage,
front protection, sustained recovery, single-target damage or multi-target coverage.
Do not invent these mechanics for mission1 merely to satisfy a difficulty label.
Recommend multiple viable kits for each required function, rather than a mandatory
named pickup, rarity check, or immunity removable only by one paid character.
Train and package choices contribute; specialization is not only replacing operators.

For upper-tier comparisons hold growth/resources approximately comparable and vary
composition, then compare appropriate composition vs mismatched composition with
the same driver. Assess survival, clear time and threat handling, not displayed
power alone. Appropriate compositions must be actually attainable under the tested
account assumptions; hypothetical access to every operator is not a free-player test.
Do not force automatic defeat on mismatched squads or scale enemies to their roster.
Overgrowth can still help; this policy introduces no hidden counter or hard power cap.

Existing entry requirements remain separate from composition advice: no new power
matchmaking filter, roster gate or top-tier admission rule. Invite carry below the
top two tiers remains allowed; weaker partner need not independently prove solo
clear ability. World boss has no difficulty, so these tier rules do not apply there.
No story difficulty selector is introduced by this section.

Acceptance extension: lowest-tier encounter progression requires initial-five P1
validation at its attainable growth; upper tiers require multiple appropriate
composition cases and matched mismatched-control cases. No win-rate or threshold
claim until those event scenarios and later playtests are actually executed.

| Group | Growth | Encounter | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Initial five L1/P0/kit1, train1 | Reference15waves/riskI | Basic behavior and time budget |
| B | L5/10/15/20/25/30 per existing reference | Mapped ordinary/story raid | Actual progression once mission tables exist |
| C | Same A, equipment/research separately enabled | Same reference | Isolate persistent modifier impact |
| D | L50/P3/kit5, train10 | Same fixed encounter | Overgrowth/overflow/fast-clear, NOT target pacing |
| E | Matched attainable growth, riskI..V | Same operation | Difficulty sensitivity, no auto scaling |
| F | Initial five, each selected ultimate | Same A | Damage/defense/repair opportunity cost |
| G | One substitute from each other verified operator | Same A | Per-kit contribution/utility, not complete combinatorial search |

Group B cannot infer enemy growth from recommendation level; needs authored mission
HP/ATK tables and exact IDs first. World Raid testing is a separate versioned
matrix:180s, infiniteHP, solo/coop authority and mode mechanics, no ordinary clear
target or story failure rule. No world release expansion from this plan.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-scripted-input-policies"></a>
#### Scripted Input Policies

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-specialization-coverage-matrix---2026-09-09"></a>
##### Specialization Coverage Matrix - 2026-09-09

Design recommendation derived from current combat-stats-v1.json kits/enemies and
chapter1-encounter-curve-v1.md. These are threat profiles, NOT the unrecovered four
basic operation types or new category IDs. They describe comparisons, not proven
winning teams. No new spawn, difficulty menu or operator skill is introduced.

| Authored threat | Primary solution to compare | Alternative / cost |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Jammer attack slow | Interrupt or focus-kill before effect | Lumen/Warden cleanse after effect; base active affects one ally, not whole squad |
| Saboteur train channel | Sera/Vex/Signal runner explicit interrupt | Focus-kill before remaining pulses, train barrier/repair to absorb error; kill deadline must be measured |
| Heavy front-two burst | Protect both actual targets and recover damage | Vex armor break plus focused damage shortens exposure; one ally shield is not two-target protection |
| Rear-targeting gunner | Reach-any focused damage with rear recovery | Compatible ally shield; front tank alone does not guarantee rear protection |
| Several interior enemies | Cinder area damage or Rail multi-target attacks | Reina/Nyx focused threat removal; slower total clear may avoid more dangerous casts |
| Exterior attrition | Legal Gun/Cargo offense and support fire | Mira/manual repair or legal Defense car buys attack time; interior damage cannot automatically hit exterior |

Kit examples are replaceable role options, not a prescribed five-operator roster.
Use only owned/unlocked alternatives in account-representative tests. Signal runner
offers explicit interrupt as a rare alternative, not equal damage or a promise that
every rare-only composition clears the top tier. Do not treat stun/attack-slow as
explicit interrupt, especially against a control-immune boss. Sera ultimate has no
interrupt. Any ultimate solution must occupy the single selected-ultimate slot.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-composition-trade-offs-to-expose"></a>
##### Composition Trade-offs To Expose

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-concrete-five-member-comparison-candidates---2026-09-09"></a>
###### Concrete Five-member Comparison Candidates - 2026-09-09

Use current combat-stats-v1.json IDs/kits, not new characters. These are proposed
test teams, NOT validated high-tier clears or player-required presets. Rear3 and
front2 below both remain inside the ally-left area. Order listed is top to bottom.

| Case | Rear3 | Front2 | One selected ultimate | Trade-off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dual interrupt | Sera, Vex, Eve | Kyle, Mira | Eve | Two explicit interrupts, mark/armor-break plus train repair; sacrifices Reina's focused burst |
| Rare interrupt focus | Reina, Signal runner, Eve | Kyle, Mira | Eve | Rare explicit interrupt and focused damage; fewer prevention opportunities than dual interrupt |
| Interior area | Cinder, Vex, Marrow | Warden, Rail | Marrow | Multi-target damage, single-ally cleanse/shield and sustained healing; no Mira train repair and delayed healing |

First compare the first two teams and initial-five control on the SAME authored
sabotage encounter with the SAME legal train/package/growth. The control is not
declared unfit by identity: it already has Sera interruption. Measure differences
instead of deliberately making it lose. Rare alternative is a coverage hypothesis,
not a guarantee it clears every high-tier case. Signal runner18s vs Sera/Vex16s
must be reflected in actual command traces, including unavailable windows.

Evaluate the third team on an existing multi-enemy interior encounter; also compare
its exterior waiting and train survival. Do not place it into an invented operation
or infer that Rail stun cancels a control-immune boss. Marrow HoT is not an immediate
full-party heal, Warden active is not whole-party cleanse, and only selected Marrow
ultimate is available in this fixture. Manual train repair remains if legally ready.

For squad-isolation keep previously proposed Guard/TrainFire/Medicine/Precision
package and matched train constant, validating Precision-compatible effects first.
Later package/ultimate changes are separate variants, not silent optimizations for
one team. Record all actor levels/promotion/kit ranks; matched level is a controlled
comparison, NOT equal acquisition cost or proof a free account owns every candidate.
Account-representative tests require actual attainable ownership/growth evidence.

Structural check only: PowerShell parsed base JSON and confirmed all three teams
have5 unique catalog operators with kits. No HP trajectory, clear-time, ownership,
role-targeting runtime or balance test performed. Missing encounter/entitlement
fixtures still block a live-valid test, not this proposed roster illustration.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-upper-difficulty-encounter-authoring-proposal---2026-09-09"></a>
###### Upper Difficulty Encounter Authoring Proposal - 2026-09-09

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-selected-ultimate-comparison-detail---2026-09-09"></a>
###### Selected Ultimate Comparison Detail - 2026-09-09

Use the same squad/train/growth/encounter and vary ONLY selected ultimate first.
Current initial-five alternatives are all present without recruitment. The table
is a test intention, not measured superiority or new kit tuning.

| Initial-five ultimate | Intended advantage | Lost alternative / limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Eve | Restore living squad HP after damage | Cannot prevent lethal hit or revive downed actors; no train repair |
| Kyle | Shield squad before a known incoming hit | Expired/unused shield contributes nothing; no recovery of existing HP loss |
| Reina | Remove priority target or shorten boss exposure | No direct squad recovery; overkill is not useful damage |
| Sera | Focus damage plus stronger mark for follow-up attacks | No ultimate interrupt; mark does not add to her active beyond strongest-source rule |
| Mira | Train repair plus temporary train damage buff | No operator recovery; separate effective repair and actual output, not total nominal buff value |

All five ordinary actives remain available regardless of ultimate selection. One
chosen ultimate only; no midbattle swap after seeing a warning, extra charge, free
cooldown reset at wave/phase change or fallback ultimate when its owner is down.
Retain existing first15s/reuse45s candidate and caster availability. Choosing an
offensive ultimate must not remove Eve's active heal from the comparison.

Existing P1 includes an Eve-specific trigger, so changing its operator ID alone is
not a fair test. Author an explicit driver per alternative, using only revealed
warnings/current targets/HP and the same decision budget. Kyle reacts to compatible
revealed incoming threats; offensive choices need a living reachable priority target;
Mira evaluates actual train missingHP and/or a legal current train-damage opportunity.
Do not read future spawn or boss pattern times, auto-cast into empty waves, or invent
damage predictions as guaranteed kill checks. Record failed/unused opportunities.

Match the observation/action budget and report cast count, effective damage/heal/
absorption/repair, actor downtime, train minimum and clear time. Different legal
trigger rules must be included in the report, not hidden as equal input traces.
Tactic stays Precision for the first comparison; Finisher is a later separately
labeled variant and must not alter buff percentage/duration or cleanse strength.

For the proposed area squad compare Marrow vs Warden: sustained healing after damage
versus shielding/cleanse before or after compatible effects. Neither gives Mira train
repair. Warden's ultimate is not immunity to all mechanics, and Marrow ticks do not
arrive instantly. Not all ultimate alternatives must be equally optimal for each
encounter; require useful distinct situations, not artificial identical clear times.

Preparation shows scope, cooldown and effect summary for the chosen operator, not a
universal Best label. Changing it invalidates only incompatible package selections
and resets readiness under existing rules. No additional ultimate-unlock economy.
Source-kit/manual policy readback only; no simulated casts or outcome measurements.

Apply only to content with an authored difficulty selector. Chapter1 story reference
tables are examples of existing threats, not permission to add tiers to story or
World. Exact four basic category IDs remain unresolved. No live roster changes.

| Candidate tier | Encounter emphasis |
| --- | --- |
| I | Initial-five coverage; existing simple composition and adequate growth |
| II | Same recognizable threats with existing numeric pressure; practice prioritization |
| III | One sustained role pressure, such as rear damage or sabotage, within the operation's authored theme |
| IV | Two complementary pressures, such as front protection plus priority-target removal |
| V | Repeated mixed-role decisions across waves with limited wasted cooldowns; no new unreadable simultaneous specials |

Do not interpret role pressure as mandatory uninterrupted control or a requirement
to cancel every warning. Successful mitigation/recovery and source removal remain
valid answers. Avoid making every operation converge to the same heavy+jammer+hound
roster; maintain its theme and let different specializations be useful across content.

Author roster replacements rather than adding enemies beyond the existing interior
cap4. Reallocate that wave's EHP budget across the replacement roster; never add a
full elite's baseHP on top of allocated waveHP. Stat multipliers apply once. Compare
numeric-only difficulty against roster-change-only before evaluating their combined
version so an excessive jump can be traced. This proposes a method, not new factors.

Retain existing major-warning scheduling: one lane token, full authored warning,
1500ms separation,4000ms maximum delay then skipped occurrence. No high-tier override
that shortens warnings, ignores the token or delivers skipped casts as catch-up.
Check the existing danger-starvation acceptance rule: additional special enemies
must not make their defining threats disappear repeatedly through queue saturation.
Ordinary attacks still occur concurrently; include their damage during warnings.

Preparation preview shows visible major threats, target scope and operation-specific
recommendations, not exact hidden schedule or guaranteed-clear percentages. A tier
change must refresh its threat/reward/cost preview and ready state according to the
existing preparation policy. Do not add an extra paid counter slot or new admission
power requirement. Keep carry and matchmaking rules unchanged.

Per-tier exit evidence must include two viable alternative compositions at attainable
growth, failure causes for the control composition, queue skips, both-lane timings
and burst overlap. Top tiers may punish repeated mistakes; full-warning visibility
and a feasible response remain required. No playtest results are claimed here.

- Adding a second interrupt improves coverage but displaces damage, healing or train
  repair; same-cooldown skills are not a free guarantee of continuous cancellation.
- Replacing direct recovery with prevention increases dependence on timing. Shields
  cannot heal damage already taken and cleanse does not restore lost attack time.
- Taking both mark sources is not additive beyond the existing mark policy/cap;
  compare actual uptime and opportunity cost, not sum displayed percentages.
- Interior burst specialization may leave exterior as the wave bottleneck. Keep
  both-lane completion, train damage and lane waiting in the report.
- A support-heavy team may survive longer yet fail to complete within observation.
  Do not add a hidden enrage/timeout merely to force the desired composition ranking.

For each applicable upper-tier authored encounter, compare at least two distinct
appropriate five-member teams and one role-mismatched control at matched attainable
growth. This is a proposed minimum test coverage, not a claim two teams already work.
Record who supplies prevention, recovery, priority damage and exterior support; roles
can overlap and no mandatory tank/healer count is imposed. Preserve fixed5 slots.

Preparation should display the actual selected encounter's major threats and the
current team's relevant functions, with scope and cooldown limitations. Missing
coverage is advice, not a new entry lock or paid-operator purchase prompt. Never show
a green guaranteed-clear badge from role counts. Do not reveal hidden enemy schedules.

Only existing mission threats supply initial examples: signal mission has jammer;
water-stop introduces sabotage; later chapters' catalog is not inferred here. Exact
upper-tier compositions/timings remain to be authored and tested before launch tuning.
Readback and source-kit comparison only; no simulator/runtime validation performed.

| Policy | Actions | Interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| P0 Basic-only | No manual skill/focus after start | Baseline pressure; not required to clear every encounter |
| P1 Reactive | React to visible threats after750ms | Main reference, not perfect-play oracle |
| P2 Delayed | Same policy after1500ms | Slower reaction sensitivity, not a disability stereotype |
| P3 One missed threat | P1 but skip one declared major warning in each block | Recovery from errors |
| P4 Cooldown spam | Use legal skills immediately when ready | Whether strategic timing actually matters |
| P5 Sustain focus | Prioritize healing/shields/repair; limited offense | Stall and repair-overlap risk |

P1 decisions use ONLY already revealed warning/current HP/readiness. Do not read
future schedules to optimize a cast. Queue/acceptance consumes reaction time as
defined by input spec. Interrupt current sabotage if ready; otherwise protect
train before next pulse or repair after missingHP exists. Ally heal below60%HP;
train repair below70%; these thresholds are test-driver choices, not game AI.
Shield reacts to a visible compatible hit; ultimate Eve when at least two living
allies below60%. Offensive actions use remaining availability. Lowest ratios and
stable IDs break ties. One decision per150ms in solo, while accepted actors still
act concurrently; this is harness input budget, NOT a game command-rate restriction.
Do not count an impossible/cooldown-blocked command as a successful defense.

Compare transport delay0/150/300ms each direction in remote-adapter tests, explicitly
not real network measurements. Reaction plus roundtrip is not the whole cast time:
windup, queue wait and server tick alignment must fit before the effect deadline.
No automatic success for a user's tap that arrived after authoritative commit.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-event-metrics"></a>
#### Event Metrics

Record targetable/spawn/kill times, wave boundary, both-lane clear time, waiting
for opposite lane, cast request/queue/start/reject/interrupt, effect application,
actual HP damage, shield absorption, effective heal/overheal, train repair,
carriage transfer, down/recovery and major-warning scheduled/delayed/skipped.
Report per-actor and per-lane contributions with denominators; attempted damage
is not effective damage. Track minimum HP and time below25% to reveal burst risk.
Shield contribution is actual absorbed damage, not all issued shield value.
Lost DPS estimate must disclose its counterfactual; do not present it as exact fact.

Invariants: HP0..max; no healing dead units; no duplicated effect/transfer; no
cooldown before cast start; original down counters maintained; no illegal target
replacement; cooldown/recovery monotonic; result once. Check each event, not just
end totals. Include ruleVersion in failures and a minimal replay trace without
tokens/account identifiers. Logs stay local and are not player telemetry by default.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-proposed-acceptance--review-thresholds"></a>
#### Proposed Acceptance / Review Thresholds

| Check | Proposed expectation | Failure handling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rule correctness | Zero invariant violations in all cases | Block adoption regardless of win/time |
| Reference A/P1 clear | Both lanes complete, train survives | Investigate before adjusting rewards/growth |
| Reference clear time | 180..240s target for A/P1 | Review pacing; do not impose artificial waits |
| Ordinary down burden | At most3 operator downs total and no same unit3+ in A/P1 | Inspect target concentration/heal access |
| Train pressure | Finish20..70%HP in A/P1 as diagnostic band | Outside band is review, not universal fail |
| One missed threat | No fullHP initial unit/train dies from that single ordinary mechanic | Check burst overlap; lowHP may still fall |
| Danger starvation | No repeated two consecutive skips for same special source | Fix composition/scheduling, not shorter warning |
| Strategic input | P1 should not be strictly worse than spam in both survival and time | Trace costs/targets, not force arbitrary advantage |
| Overgrowth | Faster clears allowed; no minimum duration gate | No forced enemy scaling to player stats |
| Sustain | No progression-free endless stall accepted as victory | Review time horizon/pressure, not fake defeat |

Train finish band does not apply to heal-heavy/overgrowth groups or encourage
unnecessary damage. P3 outcome is diagnostic; some repeated mistakes can fail.
Do not require every possible composition to match initial-five timing.
Set harness observation horizon600s ordinary/story; report NOT_COMPLETED_WITHIN_
OBSERVATION, NOT a new in-game timeout defeat. Any actual timeout needs separate policy.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-repair-and-recovery-exploit-checks"></a>
#### Repair And Recovery Exploit Checks

Existing raw reference: Mira275/22s plus manual400/30s =25.833HP/s before overheal,
but comparing against old illustrative18DPS is not a complete survivability result.
Measure actual timing, missingHP, interrupted casts, train damage, and opportunity
cost with and without each repair source and legal defensive device composition.

Compare intentional-down trace with matched no-intentional-down trace at same
loadout: total progress/score, downtime and remainingHP, not just recoveryHP gained.
If intentional collapse reliably increases reward-relevant output, block balance
adoption and revise mechanics; do not punish ordinary recovery as an exploit.
World mechanic eligibility/score under disconnect remains governed by its own
policy; no artificial personal damage requirement or auto-ban added here.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-economy-feedback-without-circular-assumptions"></a>
#### Economy Feedback Without Circular Assumptions

Current economy validation externally supplies story-progress schedules. It proves
conditional accounting, not that players can clear on those days. Next integrated
model must derive unlock progression from accepted encounter outcomes and legal
available growth, then apply offline stage changes from that point forward.
No using future clear rewards/cores to afford the attempt that unlocks them.
Report date-of-shortfall and resource, not just positive28day aggregate wallet.
Use actual stamina entry/cap/regeneration contract before calculating daily attempts;
do not silently assume unlimited repeats, ad refills or paid crystals.

Run free and premium with same opportunity/time policy; premium gains remain
earlier growth, not exclusive clear condition, extra mandatory coop quests or
different level caps. Failed-run rewards/first-clear replay use existing server
policy; this model cannot invent rewards to repair a difficult encounter.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-first-execution-packet---2026-09-09"></a>
#### First Execution Packet - 2026-09-09

Planning recommendation only. This narrows the existing matrix; it does not authorize
a harness implementation or certify candidate numbers. Read candidate precedence in
combat-design-readiness-index-v1.md before constructing any manifest. No additional
operator, item or encounter is created to fill missing source definitions.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-first-ordinary-fixture-recommendation---2026-09-09"></a>
##### First Ordinary Fixture Recommendation - 2026-09-09

Pin this one candidate before widening the matrix. It is a planning fixture, not
an assertion a live account owns these cars or the server supports this package.

| Input | First fixture |
| --- | --- |
| Encounter | opn_01_last_departure, solo,15waves, reference difficultyI coefficient1 |
| Squad | Kyle/Reina/Eve/Sera/Mira, all level1/promotion0/kit1 |
| Formation | Within ally-left area: rear top Reina/middle Sera/bottom Eve; front top Kyle/bottom Mira |
| Selected ultimate | Eve, existing15s initial/45s reuse candidate |
| Train | Level1, proposal_train_combat_v1: HP5000, armor10%, locomotiveATK60, engine65 |
| Cars | Default2 Combat+Gun, existing base durability and device definitions required |
| Package | SquadGuard, TrainFire, FieldMedicine, Precision, from start-package-selection-detail-v1.md |
| Excluded modifiers | Equipment/research OFF, pressure OFF; no extra legacy armor/fire-control or growth |
| Driver | P1 reactive first; same fixture for P0/P2/P4 comparisons |

DifficultyI here identifies the test coefficient, not a new story difficulty menu.
Train weight60/speed1.05 remains recorded, but does not change basic attack frequency
with pressure OFF. Chapter1 mission-specific wave composition replaces the older
generic waves. Its HP budgets already include1.30; never multiply1.30 a second time.
Package-off is a separately named diagnostic, not the full-package reference.

Pre-rounding arithmetic checks from existing base values and SquadGuard8%:
Kyle1512, Reina972, Eve1026, Sera993.6, Mira1080 maxHP. TrainFire gives locomotive
64.8/Gun43.2 damage before defense; Combat device excluded. These are intermediate
values, not a new rounding rule or observed runtime values. Pin the applicable
rounding/effect-order source before generating golden integer assertions. Do not
quietly round the fixtures differently from the eventual authority implementation.

Car durability/entitlement, selected package contract and effect rounding remain
explicit source gates. An independent planning model may label authored assumptions,
but cannot turn them into proof of valid live admission. No API requests from this
fixture. No free first-clear rewards or post-mission car unlocks finance this attempt.

This first ordinary case does not cover boss interrupt patterns: mission1 deliberately
has none. Boss cases need their own pre-clear growth/encounter manifest; do not reuse
level1 and infer a progression blocker from failure. No World/cooperative verdict.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-ordered-checks"></a>
##### Ordered Checks

| Stage | Fixed comparison | Exit criterion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 Fixture audit | Initial five, owned legal train, exact encounter, versions and full package choices | Every required definition explicit; otherwise BLOCKED |
| 1 Rule probes | Isolated hit/shield/heal, cast interruption, down/return and terminal event | Zero invariant violations; terminal outcome conflict resolved or affected case BLOCKED |
| 2 Ordinary baseline | Same first authored story operation, P1 then P0/P2/P4 | Ordered trace valid; compare actual clear, train minimum, downs and lane wait |
| 3 Boss baseline | Same authored boss and attainable pre-clear growth, P1 | Finite HP rules and A/B/C timing valid; no assumed first-clear rewards financing entry |
| 4 Single-error pairs | Boss P1 vs missed A, missed B, late C, separately | Attribute incremental loss and remaining pulses, not a claimed win-rate |
| 5 Recovery pairs | Sera unavailable, Eve unavailable, deliberate-down vs defensive trace | Record intervention and downtime; no new automatic skill or revive behavior |

Do not move to tuning stage2..5 when stage1 has a known correctness defect. Independent
valid cases may still run for diagnosis, but a green subset cannot certify the packet.
If the first authored encounter lacks a legal fixture, block it explicitly rather
than replace it with an invented operation or an assumed zero-cost loadout.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-reproducible-failure-injection"></a>
##### Reproducible Failure Injection

The single-error pairs suppress response to exactly one identified warning instance,
not every warning of that type. Keep other policy inputs/configuration unchanged.
For late C, record authoritative channel start and the actual interrupt effect time;
earlier pulses remain damage. An interrupt request with no successful effect is a
failed response, not a cancelled channel. If the warning never occurs, report the
case NOT_EXERCISED and require another fixture before claiming coverage.

Unavailable-actor fixtures must record onset, duration and cause as test interventions.
They are not new boss targeting rules or evidence those downs occur naturally. Keep
naturally occurring downs distinct in metrics. Compare paired outcomes using event
causes, because changed HP can legitimately change subsequent policy targets.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-balance-review-order"></a>
##### Balance Review Order

1. Fix invalid configuration, duplicate effects, wrong targets and ordering first.
2. Inspect overlap of warned threats, ordinary attacks, recovery and lane waiting.
3. Compare one declared balance parameter group at a time against the same baseline.
4. Rerun correctness and all impacted pairs after each proposed adjustment.

Do not solve a combat failure by granting extra recruited operators, future rewards,
new carriage ownership or paid growth. Basic-only need not clear; P2 or a single
mistake need not have an identical result to P1. Existing pacing bands remain review
targets, not reasons to force idle time or promise every composition can clear.

Each row reports fixture status, rule status and balance assessment separately.
Include observed time or the600s observation boundary, minimum train/operator HP,
down counts, effective healing/shielding, completed waves and unhandled threats.
The observation boundary is not a newly introduced gameplay defeat timeout.
No repeated deterministic trace is a human win-rate sample. World solo/coop remains
a separate packet; this first solo story packet cannot certify its authority/ranking.

This addition was checked against the existing acceptance plan and initial-five
counter timeline. Document readback only; no model, simulation, runtime test, video
or deployment. Candidate packet adoption and exact source fixtures remain next gates.

<a id="source-3ddf6e3a16add35f-reporting-and-implementation-gate"></a>
#### Reporting And Implementation Gate

Each report separates: structural validation / deterministic combat / transport
simulation / runtime adapter parity / device playtest / deployed behavior.
Use PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN per case with exact manifest and trace. Unverified
catalog fixtures are BLOCKED, not skipped into a green total. Human completion
rates require real distinct participants/samples, not repeated scripted runs.

This unit produced the design only. No simulation program was written or run.
Next review threshold candidates, reconcile legal carriage fixtures and missing
mission scaling, then explicitly authorize the first simulation slice. Continue
design with encounter-specific reference tables if those catalogs are available;
do not expand into World Raid production work by default.

<!-- source-body:source-3ddf6e3a16add35f:end -->

## Combat Skill Control Proposal

원출처: `WorkspaceRepo/docs/design/combat-skill-control-proposal-20260909.md`

검토·적용 경계: Retain active pending actual consolidation or explicit current-vs-candidate review: Approved control direction previewnocost/cooldowns independent; queueACK≠caststart, old3sretry explicitlyunadopted; numericscandidate, artnotkitproof.

<!-- source-body:source-28efa930bf7b4071:start -->
<a id="source-28efa930bf7b4071-combat-skill-control-proposal"></a>
### Combat Skill Control Proposal

Status: CONTROL DIRECTION APPROVED by user2026-09-09; numerical balance and
operator-kit reconciliation not finalized, no implementation order.
First reconcile existing operator/weapon catalogs; this does not silently replace
authored kits. Approved automatic basic attacks/manual skills/fixed formation retained.

<a id="source-28efa930bf7b4071-input-budget"></a>
#### Input Budget

Recommend one primary manual active per operator, automatic conditional passives,
and a compact separate train-support group. Do not add five more ultimate buttons
or a new shared mana pool before existing kits are audited. If existing ultimates
are required, design their access explicitly rather than deleting or hiding them.
Primary actives use individual cooldowns, visible on five portrait buttons.
Train support uses its own cooldowns, not another player's operator cooldown.
Actual ability count/duration/damage/energy costs remain catalog-driven and open.

<a id="source-28efa930bf7b4071-selection-and-commitment"></a>
#### Selection And Commitment

Instant/self skills: portrait tap submits activation. Target/area skill: enter
aim preview then explicit valid-target confirmation. Cancel before commit has
no cost/cooldown. Selecting a skill alone cannot spend resources or start cooldown.
Accepted activation commits once; duplicate input has no second effect. Invalid
dead/unavailable/out-of-range target rejection has no activation cost; refresh UI.
After accepted cast, interruption refund rules must be explicit per ability and
not inferred as universal full refund. Do not freeze authoritative time while aiming.
Show cooldown, target preview, disabled reason and acceptance distinctly; latency
cannot permit duplicate casts. Display effects only from accepted combat events
where server authority applies; exact transport/tick is engineering review later.

<a id="source-28efa930bf7b4071-solo-and-cooperative-roles"></a>
#### Solo And Cooperative Roles

Solo has both groups visible and sequentially solvable mechanics. Cooperative
train role controls train support, squad role controls five actives. Show partner
important readiness/cast state without giving command access. Commands do not
spend persistent credits/crystals/tickets; new combat gauges require design approval.

Next: reconcile existing active/ultimate/passive catalogs then approve control
budget, define actual cooldown/resource rules and interruption cases. No tests run.

<a id="source-28efa930bf7b4071-timing-and-cancel-proposal-not-yet-approved"></a>
#### Timing And Cancel Proposal (Not Yet Approved)

2026-09-09 follow-up: player-input-cooperation-detail-v1.md distinguishes queue
acknowledgment from cast-start and proposes no voluntary refund after cast-start.
The3s retry below is historical/unadopted, not the active stat candidate. Detailed
target/queue/gesture behavior remains proposed pending implementation review.

Use cooldown-only first for primary actives; do not introduce sharedMP. Trial
cooldown bands: damage12-16s, shield/control16-20s, recovery20-24s, train support
25-35s. Individual final values depend on effects and encounter duration; these
are test candidates, not certified balance or runtime configuration.
Normal encounter starts active skills ready; preserve cooldown across15waves.
No wave-transition reset exploit. World Raid readiness/recovery follows its own
existing rules, not implied by this ordinary-encounter proposal.
Cooldown starts at accepted cast; rejected selection costs nothing. Before effect
commit, caster incapacitation cancels and applies short3s retry lock instead of
full cooldown (candidate). After effect commit full cooldown remains. Persistent
effects/target loss require per-skill rules; no universal refund after effect.
Basic attack cooldown separate; manual skill may defer next basic attack, never
silently reset basic attack cooldown for extra hits. Combat resource truth belongs
to the authorized simulation, not animation callbacks.

Local audit: narrative15operator skill/ultimate cues and actual skill icon assets
exist. Those are presentation evidence, not proof of active/ultimate effect catalogs.
Scoped source search is not whole-repository proof of absence. Preserve ultimate
assets/cues pending actual kit design; do not declare ultimates removed.

## Combat Stat Implementation Design V1

검토·적용 경계: Retain active pending actual consolidation or explicit current-vs-candidate review: Proposed16kit numericbaseline only; detailed integerbps/ms,target/precision/caps/status/expiry/HoTterminaltick/transferactualHP andsnapshotfields. No combinelegacytrain3000 with5000. Ultimate15+45/fullpackage stale; actoridentity/art conflictnotresolvedbytable.

<!-- source-body:source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc:start -->
<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-combat-stat-implementation-design-v1"></a>
### Combat Stat Implementation Design V1

Status: PROPOSED NUMERIC BASELINE, design only, 2026-09-09.
Machine-readable source: [combat-stats-v1.json](../../../WorkspaceRepo/docs/design/combat-stats-v1.json).
This package replaces normalized example numbers ONLY when adopted after review.
It is not deployed balance, a measured clear-time guarantee, or a Unity work order.
Existing growth costs, currency, acquisition odds and reward contracts do not change.

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-scope-and-provenance"></a>
#### Scope And Provenance

- Covers all verified recruitable operators: 15 elite (including initial five) and
  rare op_signal_runner; not 21 operators. The current 21-result pool includes items.
- Source roster: Server owner worktree attendance-pass-20260907/server/packages/
  balance/src/gacha-policy.ts, launchEliteOperatorIds and launchNonEliteResults.
- Eight existing enemy resource IDs, one existing story boss, five carriage types.
- Legacy carriage HP/armor/weight/max counts and 30% transfer retained from Unity
  Train catalogs. New operator numbers, skills, device outputs and scaling are proposals.
- World boss template retains world-raid-rules.md mechanic/recovery candidates.
  Actual weekly three-boss identities/stats are not asserted complete.
- Equipment/research catalog IDs, chapter reference levels and the four operation
  category IDs require source reconciliation. Do not invent live IDs or enable
  partial data simply because JSON parses. No new release scope is implied.

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-units-and-runtime-contract"></a>
#### Units And Runtime Contract

All percentages are integer basis points (10000 = 100%); time is integer milliseconds.
HP/ATK/output are integers after growth resolution. Internal effect math uses fixed
precision, not frame-dependent floating accumulation. Proposed server simulation
step 50ms; input and animations are continuous, never player turns.

Definition fields: id, balanceVersion, hp, atk, armorBps, attackMs, reach, role,
passive, active and ultimate effects. Skill IDs derive as operatorId.active and
operatorId.ultimate. Skill rank applies to those two, not passive magnitude.
Runtime snapshot fields: entityId, definitionId, level, promotion, skillRank,
resolvedMaxHp/Atk/Armor, currentHp, shields, statuses, targetId, actionSequence,
nextBasicAt, skillReadyAt, downCount, recoveryAt and mode. No new saveable stat is
inferred from a badge or sprite. MaxHP changes do not refill HP during a fight.

Loadout and resolved stat version freeze at start. No equipment/rank changes mid-run.
Server validates ownership, progression and version; online mode simulates those
values authoritatively. Ordinary local simulation must still obey the existing
result verification contract; this document does not authorize trusting client rewards.
Reconnection restores the same snapshot/deadlines, never recalculates a new loadout.

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-persistent-stat-growth"></a>
#### Persistent Stat Growth

Reference: level1, skill1, promotion0, train1, risk I, no equipment/research.

```
HP(L,P)  = floor(baseHP  * (10000 + 400*(L-1)) * (10000 + 500*P) / 100000000)
ATK(L,P) = floor(baseATK * (10000 + 350*(L-1)) * (10000 + 500*P) / 100000000)
TrainHP(T) = floor(baseHP * (10000 + 800*(T-1)) / 10000)
TrainATK/deviceAmount(T) = floor(base * (10000 + 600*(T-1)) / 10000)
SkillScale(R) = (10000 + 800*(R-1)) / 10000
```

L1..50, P0..3, R1..5, T1..10. Promotion multiplies level growth, not
compounds per tier. Carriage HP uses TrainHP growth. Armor, attack interval,
weight, reach, passive, durations, cooldown and status strength do not grow with level.
SkillScale affects damage, healing, shield and repair magnitudes ONLY, not mark,
slow, armor break, taunt or buff percentages/durations. HP-based effects use
resolved caster/target maxHP as declared, then rank/passive, then effect caps.
Train manual skills have no separately purchased skill rank in this draft.
Level50/P3 HP multiplier3.404, ATK3.12225 before final floor; skill5 magnitude1.32.
Train10 HP multiplier1.72 and output1.54. Growth costs remain launch-economy-v1.

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-operator-base-table"></a>
#### Operator Base Table

IDs are canonical; display names/string IDs must come from localization, not this table.
Basic DPS is pre-armor, no skills/passives, purely a comparison number.

| ID suffix | HP | ATK | Armor | Basic interval | Basic DPS | Role |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| kyle | 1400 | 36 | 20% | 1.8s | 20.00 | Guard |
| reina | 900 | 50 | 5% | 1.4s | 35.71 | Striker |

| sera | 920 | 40 | 8% | 1.2s | 33.33 | Engineer |
| mira | 1000 | 30 | 10% | 1.8s | 16.67 | Support |

| nyx | 880 | 47 | 5% | 1.3s | 36.15 | Assassin |
| sable | 1600 | 32 | 22% | 2.0s | 16.00 | Guard |

Each of these has one passive, one active, one ultimate in JSON. These are proposed
combat roles, not a rewrite of published character identity. Only the selected
one-of-five ultimate is usable. Other operators keep their active and passive.
Ultimate first ready15s, then45s; tactical rewards may enhance but not unlock basic access.

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-skill-summary"></a>
#### Skill Summary

Numbers below are skill1 before passive/armor/caps. Percent ATK means caster ATK.
Multi-target coefficients are per target, not split. Full detailed targets/timings
and passives are in JSON; all-allies includes caster and excludes down entities.

| Operator | Active / CD | Selected ultimate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kyle | Lowest ally shield18% casterHP6s; taunt front2 for4s /18s | All shield22% casterHP8s |
| Reina | Focus hit400% ATK /14s | Focus hit1000% ATK |
| Eve | Lowest ally heal700% ATK /20s | All heal800% ATK |
| Sera | Hit180%, interrupt, mark10%6s /16s | Hit350%, mark20%10s |
| Mira | Train repair5% maxHP /22s | Repair10%, train damage15%10s |
| Vex | Hit250%, interrupt, armor-8pp6s /16s | Up to3 hit400%, armor-10pp8s |
| Nyx | Hit320% /14s | Hit850% |
| Sable | Self shield30%HP7s, taunt front2 for5s /20s | All shield20% casterHP10s |
| Marrow | Heal400% plus total500% over5s /22s | All total1000% over8s |
| Iris | Hit220%, mark12%8s /16s | Up to3 hit250%, mark18%10s |
| Rail | Front2 hit250%, stun1s /18s | Up to3 hit550%, stun1.5s |
| Anchor | Front2 hit180%, attack slow20%5s /18s | Up to3 hit300%, slow30%8s |
| Lumen | Lowest ally cleanse1 then heal400% /20s | All cleanse1, outgoing12%8s |
| Cinder | Up to3 hit100%, burn total200%5s /16s | Up to3 hit250%, burn total450%6s |
| Warden | Lowest shield15% casterHP6s, cleanse1 /18s | All shield18%8s, cleanse1 |
| Signal runner | Hit150%, interrupt /18s | Train damage10%8s |

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-targeting-and-action-timing"></a>
#### Targeting And Action Timing

- Ally area is LEFT: rear column left3, front column right2. Enemies remain RIGHT.
  Front priority is living front-column entities, then rear. A row is not a turn.
- Lowest HP = lowest current/max ratio, ties stable slot order. Front2/any3 select
  nearest logical slot, ties entity spawn sequence. Enemy any_ally uses rotating
  stable slot cursor, not unseeded random. Focus allowed for reachable targets.
- Basic first impact after attackMs from spawn. Windup is25% of base interval
  rounded up to50ms (enemy explicit windup overrides). Next impact interval uses
  attackMs/(1+speedBonus-slow), each category capped, rounded up to50ms.
  Basic recovery150ms fits inside the interval. No attack-cancel exploit/free hits.
- Skill windup is JSON, recovery200ms. Cooldown starts on accepted cast. Cast request
  during committed basic queues once for its recovery end; no parallel self-actions.
  Skills can delay but never reset next basic earlier than the original deadline.
- Target validation happens at acceptance and impact. Lost target before commit:
  deterministic eligible fallback; after projectile commit: no retarget, expire if
  invalid. No eligible target at acceptance means no cast/no cooldown.
- Interruption after acceptance consumes normal cooldown, including ultimate;
  earlier generic3s retry remains unadopted. Server denial is not a consumed cast.
  Ordinary hit damage does not interrupt. Bosses immune to stun/taunt, but explicitly
  interruptible casts can be interrupted. Never require a recruited interrupt for
  mandatory world mechanics; use role-specific mechanic interactions there.
- Specials first impact at periodMs after spawn; warning begins period-warning.
  Next schedule from prior impact; stun/interruption skips that occurrence with
  normal period, not catch-up burst. Sabotage pulses begin1s after warning completion.

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-damage-status-and-precision"></a>
#### Damage, Status And Precision

```
base = resolvedATK * skillCoefficient * applicableSkillScale
raw = base * (1 + cappedOutgoing) * (1 + cappedMark) * mechanicBossMultiplier
armor = clamp(baseArmor + conditionalArmor - strongestArmorBreak, 0, 0.60)
damage = floor(raw * (1 - armor))
absorbed = min(eligibleShield, damage)
hpLoss = min(currentHP, damage - absorbed)
```

Crit/dodge are disabled (chance0); crit multiplier1.5 is reserved, no random roll.
No elemental multiplier, accuracy, movement speed or numeric DEF curve at launch
baseline. Range is categorical because formation is fixed. Combat power display
is NOT matchmaking eligibility and has no invented rating formula here.

Outgoing damage buffs/passive bonuses add in one30% capped category. Mark uses
strongest source, max20%. Armor break strongest, max15 percentage points, not15%
of existing armor. Attack speed bonus max25%, strongest slow max30%. Conditional
passives evaluate at impact; strict below thresholds, not <=. Healing/repair/shield
passives apply only to their effect kinds, not damage or percentage buff strength.
Mechanic boss multiplier is a SEPARATE slot so world phase3 x1.50 is not capped
at1.30; apply to boss hits once, never multiply the resulting score again.

Shields from same source replace only with equal/higher remaining magnitude;
weaker applications cannot extend a stronger shield. Different sources share cap
40% recipient maxHP. Consume earliest expiry then source ID. Heal clamps missing
living HP, not revival. Train repair capped15% maxHP per effect after rank/passive.
Shield cannot absorb world mechanic failure35% maxHP, which uses ceil and is shown
as separate mechanic damage. Post-recovery protection is ordinary damage only.

Burn/HoT total magnitude splits into duration/tick count, first tick at tickMs,
remainder distributed one unit to earliest ticks. Same caster+skill replaces,
no duration stacking; different casters remain distinct. Snapshot ATK/rank on
application; armor/mark/world buff resolve each damage tick. Damage passives also
resolve per tick, including Cinder's burning target. Expired status inactive at
timestamp==expiry; last scheduled HoT/burn tick is an explicit terminal tick,
not proof other statuses remain active. No tick after attempt end.

Stun: strongest expiry, then5s control immunity after end; taunt uses newest valid
source and expires when source down. Cleanse priority stun > attack slow > burn,
ties earliest applied ID; does not clear boss mechanic marks or cooldown/down state.
Ties within a simulation tick use expiry/recovery then accepted input then stable
effect sequence. At world deadline end first, so hits exactly on deadline do not score.
Simultaneous lethal plus heal is therefore deterministic, not network-arrival order.

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-train-devices-and-health-categories"></a>
#### Train, Devices And Health Categories

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-precision-boundary-clarification---2026-09-09"></a>
##### Precision Boundary Clarification - 2026-09-09

Candidate extension for the first model, not a verified runtime contract. Preserve
the existing growth floor and final damage floor above. Do not floor each multiplier
or rely on Unity frame-based floating-point accumulation. Exact integer/rational
implementation and overflow bounds require owner review before runtime adoption.

- Resolve permanent growth with its published floor first. Apply the selected run
  maxHP modifier and floor once to obtain integer attempt maxHP, then initialize
  currentHP. Sera920 with SquadGuard8% becomes993, not994. Do not recalculate or refill
  maxHP when reconnecting. This explicitly narrows the earlier pre-rounding993.6 example.
- Damage retains precision through applicable coefficient/bonus/armor evaluation,
  flooring once immediately before shield absorption. Do not change existing buff
  stacking buckets or add TrainFire a second time under a different label.
- Example with no other modifiers: locomotive60, TrainFire8%, target armor5% gives
  floor(60*1.08*0.95)=61. Intermediate floor(64.8)=64 would incorrectly produce60.
  Shield20 then absorbs20 and leaves41 HP damage before the currentHP clamp.
- Recommend heal/repair/shield magnitude floor once after its applicable magnitude
  modifiers, then apply existing recipient caps/missingHP. Record effective amount
  separately from attempted amount. No minimum1 damage/healing is introduced here.
- Keep burn/HoT integer total allocation before tick distribution: total101 over5
  ticks becomes21/20/20/20/20. Damage tick armor/mark still evaluates per tick as
  above; post-defense total need not equal the pre-defense allocation. Do not carry
  rounded-away damage to another target or canceled/expired future ticks.
- Preserve explicit exceptions: World mechanic failure uses ceil, carriage transfer
  floors actual HP loss once, timing rounds by its existing tick rule. Never apply
  one global rounding helper indiscriminately to all these categories.

Golden cases must specify complete modifiers/targets and expected intermediate and
effective outputs. Include zero, near-integer boundary, capped shield, overheal,
overkill and interrupted periodic effects. Existing live behavior must be compared
before migration; no silent change to active version snapshots. Planning arithmetic
checked in PowerShell:61 vs60, Sera993, distributed total101. No event tests run.

2026-09-09 audit: train-loadout-speed-detail-v1.md found legacy TrainCoreCatalog
HP3000..4080 vs proposed5000..8600 and separate armor/fire-control bonuses.
This section is not reconciled runtime data. Never combine both growth profiles.
Default2 Combat+Gun changes ideal throughput; earlier bare-train estimate omits
device output. See follow-up source audit before implementation or simulation.

Train5000HP,10%armor,60ATK/1s. Manual support hit400%trainATK25sCD;
barrier8%maxHP6s30sCD; repair8%maxHP30sCD. First ready0, cast timings in JSON.
Up to three manual controls are presentation slots, not a new paid unlock.
Cargo speed affects locomotive/Gun automatic fire only, not manual cooldowns.
Medical80heal/8s; Combat24damage/1.6s; Gun40damage/2s;
Defense150shield6s/10s; Cargo10%speed6s/12s. Numeric device amounts scale with
train output. First pulse after full period; no instant pulse on creation/recovery.
Multiple devices resolve in stable carriage order and reselect targets after each.
No missed-pulse backlog on repair. Active projectiles/shields already emitted persist.

Carriage damage resolves its armor and shield once. Transfer is30% of actual
carriage HP loss, rounded down, once to trainTotalHP, no second armor/shield pass.
This clarifies earlier ambiguous carriageFinalDamage; trace callers before changing.
Direct train hits use train armor/shield. Operator damage never transfers.
Train repair affects trainTotalHP only; carriage recovers separately. No double heal.
Zero train HP fails ordinary/story immediately; pending repair cannot resurrect it.
Ordinary/story operator6/9/12s recovery50%HP2s protection; carriage10/15/20s40%2s.
Down counters per entity across run; wave/phase/reconnect do not reset.
World uses its separate8/12/16s60%3s policy, no ordinary train-zero failure.

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-enemies-waves-and-bosses"></a>
#### Enemies, Waves And Bosses

JSON contains eight enemy base HP/ATK/armor/attack intervals and special actions.
Ordinary15 waves use per-wave EHP budgets, not catalog HP pasted unscaled:
q = interiorEhp / sum(baseHP/(1-armor)) across wave; spawnHP=floor(baseHP*q).
Rounding deviation at most oneHP per enemy is accepted; log actual resulting EHP.
Enemy ATK remains base * difficultyATK; HP additionally * difficultyHP.
Do not multiply EHP budgets and spawnHP by the same difficulty twice.
Exterior one railbike each wave uses block EHP480/600/720/840/960, independently.
Both lanes start together. End wave when both clear;1s gap, no forced8..16s wait.
Budget normalization can make wave15 elite weaker than raw catalogHP; it remains
a behavior variant, not a second boss. Actual mission reference levels still gated.

Risk I..V HP multipliers1/1.25/1.55/1.9/2.3; ATK1/1.15/1.3/1.5/1.75.
These are combat test candidates, not economy drop multipliers or unlock policy.
No automatic enemy scaling to a player's strength; authored mission reference
levels must be supplied before assigning these tables to the actual chapter curve.
Coop does not mean two five-unit squads: own train plus partner's five operators.
No blanket x2HP or score multiplier. Mode-specific mechanics remain separate;
no validated solo/coop difficulty parity is claimed.

Story boss finite24000HP/15%armor;120hit every2.5s, special240 every14s warning4s.
HP phases60%/30%: damage1.1/1.2 and speed+10%/+20%. Current committed attack
keeps its scheduled deadline; next attack uses new interval. No HP reset/phase heal.
Special magnitude scales with phase damage; its14s period does not speed up.
Infinite world boss180s, phases remaining120/60/0; default attack90/2.5s is only
disabled template. Success x1.25/12s,x1.35/12s,x1.50/15s, one shared strongest slot.
Boss-specific armor/attack/roles/warning patterns must be reviewed against weekly
three-boss catalog. This file cannot activate a null boss ID.

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-equipment-research-and-unresolved-catalogs"></a>
#### Equipment, Research And Unresolved Catalogs

Follow-up candidate: [equipment-research-progression-v1.md](47_ECONOMY_DETAIL_CONTRACTS.md#source-6445961dcc522513)
defines four proposed modules, three research tracks and verified-six-encounter
growth references with existing costs. It does not enable this JSON's flags or
resolve missing chapter2/3 catalogs; all new keys require owner review.

Reserve additive base HP/ATK and bps HP/ATK/armor/speed modifiers, each tagged with
sourceId and version. Until verified item/research IDs and per-rank tables exist,
their enabled flags remain false and contribution exactly0. No synthetic item grant.
Do not reuse pricing profiles as combat-stat definitions. Work skills remain a
separate noncombat system until their existing definitions are reconciled.

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-validation-and-adoption-gates"></a>
#### Validation And Adoption Gates

<a id="source-5bcf7c7f9134d9bc-actual-planning-check-on-2026-09-09"></a>
##### Actual Planning Check On 2026-09-09

`node docs/design/validate-combat-stats-v1.mjs` exited0:16 operators/16 kits,
8 enemies/5 carriage types, six deliberately malformed fixtures rejected.
JSON/reference/arithmetic checks only. No Unity, server or device tests ran.
Initial five basic DPS119.714, interior ideal18000/119.714=150.358s; exterior
10800/60=180s. Ideal parallel total194s with gaps assumes continuous fire, no
overkill, no travel/cast delays, no buffs, no deaths and no device contributions.
It is not a measured match duration. Reference100DPS was illustrative and is
superseded by this base-stat calculation for this candidate only.

Key risks before adoption:
- Gun devices/support fire will shorten exterior bottleneck; area damage reduces
  interior duration. Actual3-4min needs event simulation, not the ideal quotient.
- Mira skill1/passive repairs275 per22s, manual repair400 per30s at train1.
  Together continuous ideal repair25.83HP/s exceeds earlier illustrative18DPS;
  do not certify danger/survival from that obsolete normalized incoming budget.
- Sera has33.33 basic DPS plus interrupt/mark, close to dedicated damage roles.
  Compare full rotations before accepting utility/damage tradeoff.
- Level50 growth and only2.3x riskV HP are not a chapter progression curve.
  Do not equate risk tiers with level bands or auto-scale content to player level.
- World mechanic buffs deliberately exceed ordinary outgoing cap; runtime must
  keep separate categories or phase3 reward would silently lose strength.
- All rows need character-identity review; numeric presence is not launch approval.

Run `node docs/design/validate-combat-stats-v1.mjs` for planning structural checks
and reference arithmetic. It is NOT an authoritative combat engine or playtest.
Adoption requires catalog/character review, mission reference levels, equipment
and research sources, and event-driven simulation. Then versioned implementation,
growth/down-rule migration and actual runtime tests, without silently overwriting
legacy12s/25%,20s/20%,third-wave incapacity behavior.

Required runtime cases: all16 kits at min/max growth,31-bit overflow bounds review,
partial shield/overheal, duplicate effect, cleanse/control expiry, lost target,
skill/basic scheduling, last burn tick, invulnerable hits, car transfer once,
all5 down, phase transitions, world deadline, solo/coop shared buff and reconnect.
Measure kill time and health trajectories with healing/skills/devices, manual and
idle play, high growth, elite-heavy damage and sustain-heavy teams. Check no
intentional down/recovery advantage. No simulator/device success is claimed here.
